root_cause: The selected English locale was visible in the menu while page text stayed Dutch because the runtime could receive repeated translation batch failures from the server-side AI translation path. The previous resilience change preserved the locale but deliberately swallowed failed batches, turning a backend/provider failure into a silent no-op for visitors.
prevention: Use a dedicated low-latency translation model instead of the general Sonnet reasoning model for UI translation.
Failed large translation batches must be retried as smaller bounded batches before giving up.
If no missing source string can be translated, the runtime must surface translation_unavailable instead of silently presenting an English-selected Dutch page.
Keep translation model/provider registration explicit and separate from website and portal QA models.
